entities.summary:
Tamagnino, Antonio della Porta, was an Italian sculptor of the Renaissance, known for his works in Florence and Rome from 1487 to 1520. He was a prominent figure in the Medici family's artistic circle, collaborating with artists such as Michelangelo and Leonardo da Vinci. Tamagnino's sculptures often depicted classical subjects, showcasing his skill in capturing the human form. His legacy continued in the 16th century, with artists such as Bernini drawing inspiration from his work. Tamagnino's sculptures adorned the Medici Palace in Florence, cementing his reputation as one of the greatest sculptors of the era.

Tamagnino's contributions to Renaissance art were significant, not only for his technical skill but also for his ability to convey complex emotions through his works. His sculptures, such as 'The Pietà', demonstrated a deep understanding of classical Greek and Roman art, as well as the emotional depth of Christian devotion.

The impact of Tamagnino's work can be seen in the many artists who followed in his footsteps, including Bernini, who often referenced Tamagnino's sculptures in his own work. Tamagnino's legacy extends beyond his own time, as his sculptures continue to inspire artists and art lovers to this day.
